label: Paid annual holidays
context: The minimum an employer must give each year. An employment agreement cannot give less, but it can give more.

label: Continuous employment before the annual holidays entitlement
context: An employee becomes entitled to the annual holidays after working continuously for the same employer for this long, and again after each further period.

label: Pay-as-you-go holiday pay
context: Of gross pay, paid instead of annual holidays. It can be agreed only for a fixed-term contract of less than 12 months, or for work so irregular that giving 4 weeks in the normal way is impossible in practice.

label: Most annual holidays an employee can cash up each year
context: An employee can ask to be paid instead of taking up to this much of their 4-week entitlement each year. The request must be in writing and the employer can say no.

label: Notice an employer must give of an annual closedown
context: An employer can have one annual closedown in any 12-month period and must give its employees this much notice before it starts.
